thread:
alex: Heads up — we've started seeing TS/Go clients crash when the console rollout added a new routing header `X-Route-Narrowcast`. Repro log attached:
```
Error: unknown route header: X-Route-Narrowcast
    at parseRouteHeader (client.ts:142)
    at Request.build (request.go:88)
```
This popped up in staging after the narrowcast canary. Need a plan before we flip to prod.

rachel: Oof. Which SDK versions are affected? Sounds like enum strictness.

alex: TS `@redwood/sdk@2.4.0` and Go `redwood-go v1.8.0` (internal proxy bundles). Repro: `curl -H 'X-Route-Narrowcast: aggr' https://staging-api.redwood` -> crash.

andrew: We tightened the header parsing to validate allowed values in v2.4.0. New routing mode added by infra isn't in the enum, so parsing throws. We can either revert strictness or add a permissive shim.

maria: Quota/attribution note: console expects `route-meta` to preserve tenant buckets. If we silently accept unknown headers, we should emit telemetry so console can ignore/unattribute if needed.

alex: Proposal: SDKs adopt permissive parsing + explicit fallback value for unknown headers (e.g., `UNRECOGNIZED`), and emit a telemetry counter `sdk.route.header.unrecognized`. Provide an opt-in strict mode for teams that want validation. Rollout via feature flag so we don't break prod customers.

rachel: That sounds safe. Migration path should be minor/patch release if we keep backward-compatible fallback. We should avoid a major unless we force strict validation. Also add a deprecation warning window.

andrew: Implementation sketch:
- TS: change `type RouteMode = 'aggr' | 'narrow' | ...` to `type RouteMode = string` at runtime with runtime check that maps unknown -> 'UNRECOGNIZED' + increment metric.
- Go: same, parse into string and map unknown values.
- Emit metric `sdk.route.header.unrecognized{sdk="<lang>",version="<ver>"}`.
- Add env var `REDWOOD_SDK_ROUTE_STRICT=true` to opt into strict validation.

alex: Rollout plan: patch SDK 2.4.x -> 2.4.1 with shim + telemetry. Feature flag `sdk.strict_route_header` default false. Canary release to internal infra tomorrow, monitor for 48h, then broad rollout. Deprecate lenient behavior after two releases with warnings.

maria: We also need console-side rules: ignore `sdk.route.header.unrecognized` for quota calculations and annotate affected clients in the rollouts page. Can we tag telemetry with `shim=true|false` so console can filter?

andrew: Yes. We'll attach label `shimmed:true` when mapping unknown. Also include `sdk` and `sdk_version`.

rachel: DevEx tasks: write migration doc + sample code for opt-in strictness, and a troubleshooting blurb for support. Also call out env var and how to revert.

alex: Who owns console change to treat shimmed events as neutral for quotas?

maria: I can take that. I'll add a dry-run flag so we can preview which tenants would be affected before we change billing behavior.

andrew: I'll open PRs for TS and Go SDKs today. TS patch will be small. Go needs one extra test. Will include metric emit hooks.

deploy-bot: deploy status: canary job queued for `sdk-2.4.1-shim` branch to staging cluster.

alex: Timeline recap: PRs today, staging canary tomorrow, 48h monitoring, flip rollout if green. Add deprecation RFC for strict mode in 2 weeks. Anything else?

rachel: Add a small E2E in staging that fakes new header values against popular client libs (node/go/python) so support can repro.

maria: I'll update billing docs to explain that shimmed headers won't affect quotas during transition.

andrew: I'll also add a local feature flag `REDWOOD_SDK_ROUTE_STRICT=1` to test strictness locally and a debug log line when unknown headers are encountered.

alex: Great. Thanks all — I'll file the follow-up tickets and ping infra + support once PRs are up.
